title: Sprint 2, task 3: Bargaining goes to the owner
where: A good assistant knows what it may decide and what a person must decide. Prices and deals are the owner's.
next: Go back to the portal. Your checks are running.

steps.title: Customers who want to bargain
steps.body:
In India almost every customer asks for a better price. AskMate must never promise a discount: only HomeShine's owner can. It should say the owner will reply, and keep the question for her.
Do this. Click the button. Five customers want to bargain, and AskMate treats them like product questions.

steps.title: Spot a customer who wants to bargain
steps.body: The problem. wants_bargain always says False, so no question ever reaches the owner.
steps.ask: Fill the BARGAIN list with bargaining words, and make wants_bargain say True when a question uses one.
steps.gets: a customer's question, like "Can I get a discount on Glanza?"
steps.gives: True for bargaining, False for everything else. "the cheapest wall hung toilet" is a product question, so it is False.
approach: Read the five unhappy customers. Write down the bargaining words they use: discount, offer, best price, last price, bulk.
Put those words and phrases in the BARGAIN list. Phrases are fine: "best price".
In wants_bargain, make the question small letters, then check if any phrase in BARGAIN is inside it. any(...) does this in one line.
Careful: do not add cheap or cheapest. A customer asking for the cheapest product is not bargaining.
steps.where: owner.py: the line BARGAIN = [] (keep it on one line) and the function wants_bargain. Leave note and inbox alone.
steps.done: all 19 customers are happy: the five bargainers go to the owner, and everyone else still gets their product.
hints: Which words appear in the five bargaining questions, but not in normal product questions?
BARGAIN is a list of strings. In the function, make the question small letters first, then ask if any phrase in BARGAIN is inside it.
Nearly there:  return any(phrase in q for phrase in ____)

answer.why: Small letters first, so DISCOUNT and Discount are caught too. any() is True as soon as one phrase is found. Phrases like best price are safer than single words: best alone would catch best basin for a small bathroom.

args: Can I get a discount on Glanza?
what is your last price for Amaze

steps.well_done: Bargaining goes to the owner, and product questions still get answers.

steps.title: See the owner's page
steps.body:
The owner reads these questions on /owner. It is protected by a secret token.
1. In .env, add a line ADMIN_TOKEN= followed by a long secret of your own (20 letters or more). Save. If you have no .env yet, copy .env.example to .env first.
2. Restart your app (Ctrl+C, then run the command below), ask any discount on Glanza? in the chat, then open http://127.0.0.1:8001/owner?token= followed by your secret.
3. On Render, add ADMIN_TOKEN in Environment the same way.

steps.title: Commit your change
steps.body: Type these in your second terminal:
steps.cmd:
git add .
git commit -m "Send bargaining to the owner"

steps.body: Push, and your checks start on GitHub.
